correctness.rationale: An explicit integer Smith-normal-form calculation gives 2 and 4 fixed states at exponents one and two. The identity A^4-I=4C_2 with det(C_2)=-2 and C_(j+1)=C_j(I+2^(j-1)C_j), whose right factor has odd determinant for all j>=2, establishes Smith 2-adic exponents (j,j+1) for A^(2^j)-I. This proves the fixed-state formula for all k,j. Since A^(2^k)=I modulo 2^k, all cycles have power-of-two periods and subtraction of fixed-point counts gives each exact multiplicity and total. Boundary k=1 and 2 are computed separately. The packaged brute-force checker exhausts all residue pairs at k=1,...,9 and verifies integer matrix certificates through j=14; this is finite support, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The relevant ordinary Pell theorem gives the maximal period for the seed (0,1), and closely related work studies companion-matrix order and prime-power lifting. None of the relevant inspected assertions classifies the full state set by least periods. The new exact fixed-point formula and orbit multiplicities require a separate two-adic invariant-factor analysis. Checks of equivalent words, other initial seeds, stronger period statements, and online tables found no coverage; this is a scoped best-knowledge originality judgment, not a universal negative literature certificate.

value.rationale: The chosen initial seed has long-studied modular Pell period, but the full permutation on all 2^(2k) possible seeds is a distinct natural invariant. The infinite complete cycle census classifies every least period, multiplicity and fixed-point count and exposes the stable exceptional multiplicity at period four arising from the 2-adic Smith defect. This is a motivated exact classification rather than a single numerical computation or a relabeling of the standard maximal Pell period.
